text: In 1910, the Antarctic Nimrod Expedition was in trouble.
ipa: /ɪn 1910 ðə æntˈɑɹktɪk nˈɪmɹɑd ˌɛkspədˈɪʃən wˈɑz ɪn tɹˈʌbəl/
vi: Năm 1910, Đoàn thám hiểm Nimrod ở Nam Cực gặp khó khăn.

text: Led by Ernest Shackleton, the team had set the record for the southernmost point ever reached.
ipa: /lˈɛd bˈaɪ ˈɝnəst ʃˈækəltən ðə tˈim hˈæd sˈɛt ðə ɹəkˈɔɹd fˈɔɹ ðə sˈʌðɚnmˌoʊst pˈɔɪnt ˈɛvɚ ɹˈitʃt/
vi: Được dẫn dắt bởi Ernest Shackleton, đội đã lập kỷ lục về điểm cực nam nhất từng đạt tới.

text: But after miscalculating how long it would take to return to the nearest supply depot,
ipa: /bˈʌt ˈæftɚ miscalculating hˈaʊ lˈɔŋ ˈɪt wˈʊd tˈeɪk tˈu ɹɪtˈɝn tˈu ðə nˈɪɹəst səplˈaɪ dˈipoʊ/
vi: Nhưng sau khi tính toán sai thời gian cần thiết để quay trở lại kho tiếp tế gần nhất,

text: the crew had run out of food.
ipa: /ðə kɹˈu hˈæd ɹˈʌn ˈaʊt ˈʌv fˈud/
vi: thủy thủ đoàn đã hết lương thực.

text: Fatigued and desperate, they turned to their medical kit.
ipa: /fətˈiɡd ənd dˈɛspɹɪt ðˈeɪ tˈɝnd tˈu ðˈɛɹ mˈɛdəkəl kˈɪt/
vi: Mệt mỏi và tuyệt vọng, họ quay sang bộ dụng cụ y tế của mình.

text: It contained a drug called “Forced March tablets,” which promised to mitigate hunger
ipa: /ˈɪt kəntˈeɪnd ə dɹˈʌɡ kˈɔld fˈɔɹst mˈɑɹtʃ tˈæbləts wˈɪtʃ pɹˈɑməst tˈu mˈɪtəɡˌeɪt hˈʌŋɡɚ/
vi: Nó chứa một loại thuốc gọi là "viên nén Bước Tiến Cưỡng Bách", hứa hẹn giảm bớt cơn đói

text: and prolong endurance, thanks to the powerful combination of its two ingredients: cocaine,
ipa: /ənd pɹəlˈɔŋ ˈɛndɚəns θˈæŋks tˈu ðə pˈaʊɚfəl kˌɑmbənˈeɪʃən ˈʌv ˈɪts tˈu ˌɪnɡɹˈidiənts koʊkˈeɪn/
vi: và kéo dài sức bền, nhờ sự kết hợp mạnh mẽ của hai thành phần: cocaine,

text: and the extract of the African kola nut.
ipa: /ənd ðə ˈɛkstɹˌækt ˈʌv ðə ˈæfɹəkən kola nˈʌt/
vi: và chiết xuất hạt kola châu Phi.

text: After taking the pills, the team was able to push through and reach safety.
ipa: /ˈæftɚ tˈeɪkɪŋ ðə pˈɪlz ðə tˈim wˈɑz ˈeɪbəl tˈu pˈʊʃ θɹˈu ənd ɹˈitʃ sˈeɪfti/
vi: Sau khi uống thuốc, đội đã có thể vượt qua và đến được nơi an toàn.

text: So how did the kola nut, a sacred ingredient from West Africa, end up
ipa: /sˈoʊ hˈaʊ dˈɪd ðə kola nˈʌt ə sˈeɪkɹəd ˌɪnɡɹˈidiənt fɹˈʌm wˈɛst ˈæfɹəkɑ ˈɛnd ˈʌp/
vi: Vậy làm thế nào mà hạt kola, một nguyên liệu thiêng liêng từ Tây Phi, lại kết thúc

text: in Shackleton's emergency kit?
ipa: /ɪn ʃˈækəltənz ɪmˈɝdʒənsi kˈɪt/
vi: trong bộ dụng cụ khẩn cấp của Shackleton?

text: And how did this same combination of kola nut
ipa: /ənd hˈaʊ dˈɪd ðˈɪs sˈeɪm kˌɑmbənˈeɪʃən ˈʌv kola nˈʌt/
vi: Và làm thế nào mà sự kết hợp tương tự của hạt kola

text: and cocaine make its way into the original recipe of a drink
ipa: /ənd koʊkˈeɪn mˈeɪk ˈɪts wˈeɪ ˈɪntu ðə ɚˈɪdʒənəl ɹˈɛsəpi ˈʌv ə dɹˈɪŋk/
vi: và cocaine có mặt trong công thức ban đầu của một loại đồ uống

text: that billions of people consume every day?
ipa: /ðˈæt bˈɪljənz ˈʌv pˈipəl kənsˈum ˈɛvɚi dˈeɪ/
vi: mà hàng tỷ người tiêu thụ mỗi ngày?

text: The kola nut is the seed of the kola tree, a small evergreen native
ipa: /ðə kola nˈʌt ˈɪz ðə sˈid ˈʌv ðə kola tɹˈi ə smˈɔl ˈɛvɚɡɹˌin nˈeɪtɪv/
vi: Hạt côla là hạt của cây côla, một loại cây thường xanh nhỏ có nguồn gốc

text: to the tropical forests of West Africa, where it has long been integral to the cultural
ipa: /tˈu ðə tɹˈɑpɪkəl fˈɔɹəsts ˈʌv wˈɛst ˈæfɹəkɑ wˈɛɹ ˈɪt hˈæz lˈɔŋ bˈɪn ˈɪntəɡɹəl tˈu ðə kˈʌltʃɚəl/
vi: đến các khu rừng nhiệt đới Tây Phi, nơi nó đã gắn bó lâu đời với văn hóa

text: fabric of many communities.
ipa: /fˈæbɹɪk ˈʌv mˈɛni kəmjˈunətiz/
vi: tấm vải của nhiều cộng đồng.

text: Among the Igbo, the bitter nut is known as the food of the gods.
ipa: /əmˈʌŋ ðə igbo ðə bˈɪtɚ nˈʌt ˈɪz nˈoʊn ˈæz ðə fˈud ˈʌv ðə ɡˈɑdz/
vi: Trong số người Igbo, hạt đắng được biết đến là thức ăn của các vị thần.

text: In Igbo homes, its custom to greet and honor guests by breaking a seed
ipa: /ɪn igbo hˈoʊmz ˈɪts kˈʌstəm tˈu ɡɹˈit ənd ˈɑnɚ ɡˈɛsts bˈaɪ bɹˈeɪkɪŋ ə sˈid/
vi: Trong các gia đình Igbo, phong tục chào hỏi và tôn vinh khách bằng cách bẻ một hạt giống.

text: and sharing the lobes.
ipa: /ənd ʃˈɛɹɪŋ ðə lˈoʊbz/
vi: và chia sẻ các thùy.

text: Within Yoruba communities, kola plays a central role in many religious ceremonies, such
ipa: /wɪðˈɪn jəɹˈubə kəmjˈunətiz kola plˈeɪz ə sˈɛntɹəl ɹˈoʊl ɪn mˈɛni ɹɪlˈɪdʒəs sˈɛɹəmˌoʊniz sˈʌtʃ/
vi: Trong cộng đồng Yoruba, hạt kola đóng vai trò trung tâm trong nhiều nghi lễ tôn giáo, chẳng hạn như

text: as weddings, funerals, and divination.
ipa: /ˈæz wˈɛdɪŋz fjˈunɚəlz ənd dˌɪvənˈeɪʃən/
vi: như đám cưới, đám tang và bói toán.

text: Kola nuts can contain up to 2.5% caffeine,
ipa: /kola nˈʌts kˈæn kəntˈeɪn ˈʌp tˈu 25 kæfˈin/
vi: Hạt kola có thể chứa tới 2,5% caffeine,

text: or about twice the concentration found in coffee beans, along with trace amounts of theobromine,
ipa: /ˈɔɹ əbˈaʊt twˈaɪs ðə kˌɑnsəntɹˈeɪʃən fˈaʊnd ɪn kˈɑfi bˈinz əlˈɔŋ wˈɪð tɹˈeɪs əmˈaʊnts ˈʌv theobromine/
vi: hoặc gấp đôi nồng độ tìm thấy trong hạt cà phê, cùng với một lượng nhỏ theobromine,

text: a structurally similar compound.
ipa: /ə stɹˈʌktʃɚəli sˈɪməlɚ kˈɑmpaʊnd/

text: Both molecules stimulate the central nervous system, causing effects like alertness
ipa: /bˈoʊθ mˈɑləkjˌulz stˈɪmjəlˌeɪt ðə sˈɛntɹəl nˈɝvəs sˈɪstəm kˈɑzɪŋ ɪfˈɛkts lˈaɪk əlˈɝtnəs/

text: and increased blood flow to the muscles and lungs.
ipa: /ənd ˌɪnkɹˈist blˈʌd flˈoʊ tˈu ðə mˈʌsəlz ənd lˈʌŋz/

text: And it’s these properties that likely led to kola’s long-standing use in traditional West African medicine.
ipa: /ənd ˈɪts ðˈiz pɹˈɑpɚtiz ðˈæt lˈaɪkli lˈɛd tˈu kolas lˈɔŋstˌændɪŋ jˈus ɪn tɹədˈɪʃənəl wˈɛst ˈæfɹəkən mˈɛdəsən/

text: But there’s also a bitter side to the kola nut’s history.
ipa: /bˈʌt theres ˈɔlsoʊ ə bˈɪtɚ sˈaɪd tˈu ðə kola nˈʌts hˈɪstɚi/

text: As early as the 10th century, it was used by various groups in West Africa
ipa: /ˈæz ˈɝli ˈæz ðə 10th sˈɛntʃɚi ˈɪt wˈɑz jˈuzd bˈaɪ vˈɛɹiəs ɡɹˈups ɪn wˈɛst ˈæfɹəkɑ/

text: as currency to purchase captives across the Sahara.
ipa: /ˈæz kˈɝənsi tˈu pˈɝtʃəs kˈæptɪvz əkɹˈɔs ðə səhˈɛɹə/

text: And in the 16th century, Portuguese and Afro-Portuguese traders in the region similarly exchanged the seeds
ipa: /ənd ɪn ðə 16th sˈɛntʃɚi pˈɔɹtʃəɡˌiz ənd afroportuguese tɹˈeɪdɚz ɪn ðə ɹˈidʒən sˈɪməlɚli ɪkstʃˈeɪndʒd ðə sˈidz/

text: for people, whom they then sold into transatlantic slavery.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ pˈipəl hˈum ðˈeɪ ðˈɛn sˈoʊld ˈɪntu tɹˌænzətlˈæntɪk slˈeɪvɚi/

text: By the 17th century, the kola nut had made its way to the Americas.
ipa: /bˈaɪ ðə 17th sˈɛntʃɚi ðə kola nˈʌt hˈæd mˈeɪd ˈɪts wˈeɪ tˈu ðə əmˈɛɹəkəz/

text: Brazilian oral narratives tell of enslaved peoples smuggling the seeds across the Atlantic
ipa: /bɹəzˈɪljən ˈɔɹəl nˈæɹətɪvz tˈɛl ˈʌv ɛnslˈeɪvd pˈipəlz smˈʌɡlɪŋ ðə sˈidz əkɹˈɔs ðə ətlˈæntɪk/

text: in their clothing and hair.
ipa: /ɪn ðˈɛɹ klˈoʊðɪŋ ənd hˈɛɹ/

text: Enslavers who learned of the nut’s energizing properties often weaponized
ipa: /enslavers hˈu lˈɝnd ˈʌv ðə nˈʌts ˈɛnɚdʒˌaɪzɪŋ pɹˈɑpɚtiz ˈɔfən weaponized/

text: it. Supplying it to subjugated workers to induce more back-breaking labor.
ipa: /ˈɪt səplˈaɪɪŋ ˈɪt tˈu sˈʌbdʒəɡˌeɪtɪd wˈɝkɚz tˈu ˌɪndˈus mˈɔɹ bˈækbɹˌeɪkɪŋ lˈeɪbɚ/

text: However, in places like Jamaica, Cuba, and Brazil, many enslaved communities managed to cultivate kola
ipa: /hˌaʊˈɛvɚ ɪn plˈeɪsəz lˈaɪk dʒəmˈeɪkə kjˈubə ənd bɹəzˈɪl mˈɛni ɛnslˈeɪvd kəmjˈunətiz mˈænədʒd tˈu kˈʌltəvˌeɪt kola/

text: on their own, allowing them to preserve and continue practicing their cultural and religious traditions.
ipa: /ˈɑn ðˈɛɹ ˈoʊn əlˈaʊɪŋ ðˈɛm tˈu pɹəzˈɝv ənd kəntˈɪnju pɹˈæktəsɪŋ ðˈɛɹ kˈʌltʃɚəl ənd ɹɪlˈɪdʒəs tɹədˈɪʃənz/

text: In the late 19th century, the kola nut gained the attention of pharmacists
ipa: /ɪn ðə lˈeɪt 19th sˈɛntʃɚi ðə kola nˈʌt ɡˈeɪnd ðə ətˈɛnʃən ˈʌv fˈɑɹməsɪsts/

text: in Europe and North America.
ipa: /ɪn jˈʊɹəp ənd nˈɔɹθ əmˈɛɹəkə/

text: Many claimed, without much evidence, that the nut contained countless medicinal and even mind-altering properties.
ipa: /mˈɛni klˈeɪmd wɪθˈaʊt mˈʌtʃ ˈɛvədəns ðˈæt ðə nˈʌt kəntˈeɪnd kˈaʊntləs mədˈɪsənəl ənd ˈivɪn mindaltering pɹˈɑpɚtiz/

text: Soon, kola-containing tonics, chocolates, and lozenges lined pharmacy shelves.
ipa: /sˈun kolacontaining tˈɑnɪks tʃˈɔkləts ənd lˈɔzəndʒəz lˈaɪnd fˈɑɹməsi ʃˈɛlvz/

text: It was combined with extracts from the coca leaf, the source of cocaine, to create Shackleton’s
ipa: /ˈɪt wˈɑz kəmbˈaɪnd wˈɪð ˈɛkstɹˌækts fɹˈʌm ðə kˈoʊkə lˈif ðə sˈɔɹs ˈʌv koʊkˈeɪn tˈu kɹiˈeɪt ʃˈækəltənz/

text: Forced March tablets, which were also supplied to British soldiers during World War I. In 1886,
ipa: /fˈɔɹst mˈɑɹtʃ tˈæbləts wˈɪtʃ wˈɝ ˈɔlsoʊ səplˈaɪd tˈu bɹˈɪtɪʃ sˈoʊldʒɚz dˈʊɹɪŋ wˈɝld wˈɔɹ ˈaɪ ɪn 1886/

text: Atlanta pharmacist John Pemberton used this same potent combo to create the original recipe
ipa: /ætlˈæntə fˈɑɹməsɪst dʒˈɑn pˈɛmbɚtən jˈuzd ðˈɪs sˈeɪm pˈoʊtənt kˈɑmbˌoʊ tˈu kɹiˈeɪt ðə ɚˈɪdʒənəl ɹˈɛsəpi/

text: for Coca-Cola, which he claimed could treat ailments like headaches, indigestion, and impotence.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ cocacola wˈɪtʃ hˈi klˈeɪmd kˈʊd tɹˈit ˈeɪlmənts lˈaɪk hˈɛdˌeɪks ˌɪndaɪdʒˈɛstʃən ənd ˈɪmpətəns/

text: By the 1920s, African export of the kola nut slowed, thanks in part to the introduction
ipa: /bˈaɪ ðə 1920s ˈæfɹəkən ˈɛkspɔɹt ˈʌv ðə kola nˈʌt slˈoʊd θˈæŋks ɪn pˈɑɹt tˈu ðə ˌɪntɹədˈʌkʃən/

text: of another energizing seed from the region: the cocoa bean.
ipa: /ˈʌv ənˈʌðɚ ˈɛnɚdʒˌaɪzɪŋ sˈid fɹˈʌm ðə ɹˈidʒən ðə kˈoʊkoʊ bˈin/

text: Around this time, the Coca-Cola company is also said to have significantly reduced the kola nut
ipa: /ɚˈaʊnd ðˈɪs tˈaɪm ðə cocacola kˈʌmpənˌi ˈɪz ˈɔlsoʊ sˈɛd tˈu hˈæv sɪɡnˈɪfɪkəntli ɹədˈust ðə kola nˈʌt/

text: in its recipe, but no one knows for sure— the exact ingredients remain
ipa: /ɪn ˈɪts ɹˈɛsəpi bˈʌt nˈoʊ wˈʌn nˈoʊz fˈɔɹ ʃˈʊɹ ðə ɪɡzˈækt ˌɪnɡɹˈidiənts ɹɪmˈeɪn/

text: a closely guarded trade secret.
ipa: /ə klˈoʊsli ɡˈɑɹdəd tɹˈeɪd sˈikɹət/

text: However, we do know that the company removed all traces of cocaine by 1903.
ipa: /hˌaʊˈɛvɚ wˈi dˈu nˈoʊ ðˈæt ðə kˈʌmpənˌi ɹimˈuvd ˈɔl tɹˈeɪsəz ˈʌv koʊkˈeɪn bˈaɪ 1903/

text: Today, the kola nut can still be found in various drinks
ipa: /tədˈeɪ ðə kola nˈʌt kˈæn stˈɪl bˈi fˈaʊnd ɪn vˈɛɹiəs dɹˈɪŋks/

text: and supplements, like Bissy tea, a staple in many Jamaican homes.
ipa: /ənd sˈʌpləmənts lˈaɪk bissy tˈi ə stˈeɪpəl ɪn mˈɛni dʒəmˈeɪkən hˈoʊmz/

text: Believed to have been first brought to the region on slave ships in the 17th century,
ipa: /bɪlˈivd tˈu hˈæv bˈɪn fˈɝst bɹˈɔt tˈu ðə ɹˈidʒən ˈɑn slˈeɪv ʃˈɪps ɪn ðə 17th sˈɛntʃɚi/

text: this tea is just one example of how the kola nut, despite its bitter past, continues
ipa: /ðˈɪs tˈi ˈɪz dʒˈʌst wˈʌn ɪɡzˈæmpəl ˈʌv hˈaʊ ðə kola nˈʌt dɪspˈaɪt ˈɪts bˈɪtɚ pˈæst kəntˈɪnjuz/

text: to serve as a powerful symbol of cultural preservation and remembrance.
ipa: /tˈu sˈɝv ˈæz ə pˈaʊɚfəl sˈɪmbəl ˈʌv kˈʌltʃɚəl pɹˌɛzɚvˈeɪʃən ənd ɹimˈɛmbɹəns/
